subject: Pathology
subtopic: Immune checkpoint inhibitors and tumor immunology
vignette: A 68-year-old man with metastatic melanoma is started on ipilimumab, an antibody directed against an inhibitory receptor on T cells. Four weeks later he develops profuse watery diarrhea, abdominal cramping, and a pruritic maculopapular rash. Stool studies are negative for pathogens. His oncologist attributes these symptoms to the mechanism of the drug rather than to infection.
question: Which of the following best explains both the antitumor effect and the adverse effects of this drug?

options.text: CTLA-4 on T cells outcompetes CD28 for B7 on antigen-presenting cells, and blocking it restores T-cell costimulation, which can also attack normal tissue
The drug blocks PD-L1 on tumor cells, preventing PD-1 engagement and T-cell exhaustion
The drug depletes regulatory T cells by binding CD25 and causes autoimmunity through interleukin-2 deficiency
The drug directly kills tumor cells by cross-linking B7 on the tumor surface
The drug increases MHC class I expression on tumor cells, allowing cytotoxic T-cell recognition

explanation_correct: Immune checkpoint interactions modulate T-cell activation and normally decrease the immune response against tumor cells. CTLA-4 on T cells outcompetes CD28 for B7 on antigen-presenting cells, producing loss of the T-cell costimulatory signal; ipilimumab blocks CTLA-4 and restores costimulation. Because checkpoint blockade unleashes the immune response nonselectively, immune-related adverse events such as colitis, dermatitis, and endocrinopathies occur.

explanation_incorrect.B: That describes antibodies against PD-L1 such as atezolizumab, durvalumab, or avelumab, or antibodies against PD-1 such as nivolumab and pembrolizumab, not a CTLA-4 antibody.
explanation_incorrect.C: Regulatory T-cell depletion via CD25 binding describes agents such as basiliximab used in transplantation, and interleukin-2 deficiency is not the checkpoint mechanism.
explanation_incorrect.D: Checkpoint inhibitors work by modulating T-cell signaling rather than by directly killing tumor cells through B7 cross-linking.
explanation_incorrect.E: Inducing MHC class I expression is not the mechanism, and tumor cells typically decrease MHC class I to escape cytotoxic T cells.

educationalObjective: Ipilimumab blocks CTLA-4, restoring T-cell costimulation by preventing CTLA-4 from outcompeting CD28 for B7.

subject: Pathology
subtopic: Immune checkpoint inhibitors and tumor immunology
vignette: A 71-year-old woman with metastatic lung adenocarcinoma receives pembrolizumab, an antibody directed against PD-1. Her scans show significant tumor regression. After several cycles she develops fatigue, proximal muscle weakness, and an elevated TSH with low free T4, along with a mild diffuse skin rash. Her oncologist explains that these are immune-related effects rather than metastatic spread.
question: Which of the following best describes the interaction targeted by this therapy?

options.text: CTLA-4 binding B7 on the T cell, preventing CD28 signaling
PD-1 on T cells interacting with PD-L1 or PD-L2 on tumor cells or immune cells in the tumor microenvironment, causing T-cell dysfunction or exhaustion
MHC class II on antigen-presenting cells interacting with the T-cell receptor to trigger apoptosis
B7 on the antigen-presenting cell engaging CD28 to inhibit T-cell activation
Tumor cells secreting transforming growth factor beta to recruit regulatory T cells

explanation_correct: PD-1 on T cells engages PD-L1 or PD-L2 expressed by tumor cells or immune cells in the tumor microenvironment, producing T-cell dysfunction known as exhaustion and reducing the immune response against tumor cells. Antibodies against PD-1 (cemiplimab, nivolumab, pembrolizumab) or against PD-L1 (atezolizumab, durvalumab, avelumab) block this interaction. Because the blockade is systemic, immune-related adverse effects such as endocrinopathy, dermatitis, and colitis can emerge.

explanation_incorrect.A: This describes the CTLA-4 pathway targeted by ipilimumab, and the geometry in the option wrongly places B7 on the T cell.
explanation_incorrect.C: MHC class II presents antigen to the T-cell receptor to activate CD4-positive T cells rather than to trigger apoptosis, and it is not the checkpoint targeted here.
explanation_incorrect.D: B7 engaging CD28 normally provides a positive costimulatory signal, so it is the opposite of an inhibitory checkpoint.
explanation_incorrect.E: TGF-beta secretion and regulatory T-cell recruitment are genuine tumor escape mechanisms but are not the interaction blocked by anti-PD-1 therapy.

educationalObjective: Anti-PD-1 and anti-PD-L1 agents block PD-1/PD-L1 signaling that otherwise exhausts T cells against the tumor.

subject: Pathology
subtopic: Immune checkpoint inhibitors and tumor immunology
vignette: A 60-year-old man with metastatic renal cell carcinoma has progressed despite checkpoint inhibitor therapy. Analysis of his tumor tissue shows markedly reduced membranous MHC class I expression on the tumor cells, a dense infiltrate of regulatory T cells, and high stromal levels of transforming growth factor beta. His oncologist explains that these findings represent immune escape.
question: Which of the following best explains why this tumor escapes immune-mediated destruction?

options.text: High MHC class I expression prevents cytotoxic T cells from recognizing the tumor
Reactivation of telomerase directly suppresses T-cell function in the tumor microenvironment
Reduced MHC class I expression prevents recognition by cytotoxic T cells, and immunosuppressive factors plus regulatory T cells dampen the response
The Warburg effect produces lactate that specifically activates cytotoxic T cells against benign tissue
Loss of E-cadherin enables tumor cells to present tumor antigens more efficiently to T cells

explanation_correct: Tumor cells must evade immune destruction for successful tumorigenesis, and they do so by several mechanisms: decreased MHC class I expression so cytotoxic T cells cannot recognize them, secretion of immunosuppressive factors such as transforming growth factor beta, recruitment of regulatory T cells to downregulate the immune response, and upregulation of immune checkpoint molecules. All three findings in this vignette are classic escape mechanisms.

explanation_incorrect.A: The relationship is inverted; reduced rather than high MHC class I expression is the escape mechanism, and high expression would make recognition easier.
explanation_incorrect.D: The Warburg effect supplies carbon for biosynthesis and increases lactic acid production, but it does not activate cytotoxic T cells.
explanation_incorrect.E: Loss of E-cadherin promotes invasion and metastasis rather than improving antigen presentation, which is a feature of antigen-presenting cells.
explanation_incorrect.B: Telomerase reactivation confers limitless replicative potential and does not suppress T-cell function in the microenvironment.

educationalObjective: Tumors escape immunity by decreasing MHC class I, secreting immunosuppressive TGF-beta, recruiting regulatory T cells, and upregulating checkpoints.
